# 

# Assemble Process

So the assemble process was sort of straightforward. It was not easy to do, but even without a manual (that did not came) you should be able to figure out what piece goes where. We were in 4 persons, we started just after lunch (about 1PM) and took us about 6 – 7 hours to get it assembled.

![Metal satellite dish antenna mounted on rooftop, surrounded by buildings and wires.](/assets/goes-satellite-hunt/30117195250_d6ea68bbae_z.jpg)

![White metal antenna with multiple curved arms, mounted outdoors near concrete wall and debris.](/assets/goes-satellite-hunt/30117193780_c128f0ac0c_z.jpg)

![Large metal mesh satellite dish leaning indoors on concrete floor](/assets/goes-satellite-hunt/30414297785_9d42822a51_z.jpg) ![Metal fan blade assembly with mesh guard, mounted on a pole with bolts and brackets.](/assets/goes-satellite-hunt/29782514093_ddeddb12cc_z.jpg)

![Concrete floor with four drilled holes, white powder dust, and a power drill nearby.](/assets/goes-satellite-hunt/30117198940_0bce266ed2_z.jpg)

I also decided to inject Polyurethane Foam into the dish tube, so when it rains it doesn’t get filled with water. The only tip I have is: Be careful, your dish can grow balls.

![White, lumpy masses hanging from a metal mesh structure at night.](/assets/goes-satellite-hunt/29782515453_b69e273037_z.jpg)

So the dish assemble is done. Now we need to worry about the feed.
